I was born in Nigeria, and raised and educated in New Jersey and New York City. But more than a decade ago, my journey led me to the heart of the Mississippi Delta, a region whose rich history, resilience, hope, and deeply-rooted bloodlines tell a powerful American story. I arrived because I recognized an unmet healthcare need that could no longer be ignored—a disturbing pattern of preventable limb loss that I came to describe as the Black American amputation epide…
